stories.title: Coldcard exploit fuels debate over hardware wallet security
stories.summary: A newly disclosed exploit against Coldcard hardware wallets has raised questions about self-custody security, with some analysts telling CoinDesk it could push more investors toward regulated bitcoin exposure like ETFs rather than self-custody. Cointelegraph separately examined whether the attack implicates hardware wallets broadly or is specific to Coldcard's design.
stories.whyItMatters: Security scares around self-custody tools can shift capital toward regulated products, affecting flows into bitcoin ETFs and custodial services.
whatToWatch: Whether Coldcard or independent researchers publish a technical post-mortem
Responses from other hardware wallet makers
Any visible shift in flows toward regulated bitcoin products
questions: Is the vulnerability specific to Coldcard's architecture or a broader hardware wallet risk?
Has any user actually lost funds in the exploit?

sources.title: Coldcard exploit could boost demand for regulated bitcoin exposure, analysts say
Do the Coldcard attacks mean all hardware wallets are now insecure?

stories.title: XRP whales keep buying the dip while ether shows deeper capitulation
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports large XRP holders continuing to accumulate through the recent pullback, while ether's price action points to more pronounced capitulation among its holders. The divergence suggests investor conviction is holding up better for XRP than for ETH in the current downturn.
stories.whyItMatters: Whale accumulation patterns are a closely watched signal for where conviction, or fear, is concentrated across major tokens during a drawdown.
whatToWatch: Whether XRP whale buying continues if prices fall further
Any stabilization in ether's on-chain selling pressure
questions: How much of the XRP buying is exchange-based versus long-term wallet accumulation?

stories.title: CASHCAT surges 120% as Robinhood Chain's value locked tops $774 million
stories.summary: The token CASHCAT rallied 120% over the past week as Robinhood Chain's total value locked climbed to $774 million, according to CoinDesk. The move highlights fast-growing activity on the newer chain even as broader crypto markets have been choppy.
stories.whyItMatters: Rapid TVL growth and token spikes on emerging chains like Robinhood Chain signal where speculative capital and developer activity are migrating.
whatToWatch: Whether Robinhood Chain's TVL growth holds or reverses
Whether CASHCAT's rally sustains or gives back gains
questions: What specifically is driving demand for CASHCAT versus other tokens on the chain?

stories.title: Bitcoin Red Team audit surfaces roughly 5,000 findings
stories.summary: A sweeping security audit conducted by the Bitcoin Red Team turned up around 5,000 findings, according to Cointelegraph. Initial reporting did not specify a severity breakdown or exactly which parts of the ecosystem were covered.
stories.whyItMatters: Large-scale security reviews of core Bitcoin infrastructure matter for tracking protocol-level risk, even before findings are triaged into confirmed vulnerabilities.
whatToWatch: A breakdown of critical versus low-severity findings
Any disclosed fixes or patches resulting from the audit
questions: How many of the 5,000 findings represent genuine vulnerabilities versus minor or informational issues?
Which projects or components were in scope?

stories.title: Bitcoin lags as global equities hit record highs; chipmaker's BTC sale wipes out its debt
stories.summary: Bitcoin and the broader crypto market failed to keep pace as global equity indexes set fresh record highs, according to CoinDesk. Separately, CryptoSlate reported that a cellular chipmaker sold off 1,200 bitcoin from its treasury, using the proceeds to erase its debt and roughly double its cash position.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's underperformance against equities and a corporate treasury unwinding its BTC holdings both speak to how institutional and public-company sentiment toward bitcoin exposure is evolving.
whatToWatch: Whether other corporate bitcoin treasuries make similar sales
Whether bitcoin's relative underperformance versus equities persists
questions: Which chipmaker sold the bitcoin, and does the move signal a broader trend among public companies holding BTC treasuries?

stories.title: ElizaOS token hits record low after founder calls project 'dead'
stories.summary: The ElizaOS token fell 19% to a record low after its founder publicly declared the project dead, according to Cointelegraph. The statement triggered a sharp selloff among remaining holders.
stories.whyItMatters: Founder-declared project failures are a reminder of how concentrated and reflexive risk remains in smaller AI-crypto tokens.
whatToWatch: Whether the founder or team issues a formal wind-down plan or further clarification
Any attempt by the community to fork or revive the project
questions: What specifically prompted the founder to call the project dead?

stories.title: Bitcoin holds above $64,000 as traders eye $100 billion SpaceX unlock
stories.summary: Bitcoin steadied above $64,000, with traders reportedly watching a $100 billion SpaceX unlock event, according to CoinDesk. The report ties broader risk sentiment to the looming unlock, though details on its exact mechanics weren't specified.
stories.whyItMatters: Large unlock events tied to major private companies can inject volatility into risk assets, including crypto, depending on how any resulting liquidity is deployed.
whatToWatch: The actual timing and mechanics of the SpaceX unlock
Bitcoin's price reaction once the unlock occurs
questions: What form does the SpaceX unlock take, and why is it being linked to bitcoin specifically?

stories.title: US Solana ETFs post five straight days of zero net flows
stories.summary: All six US-listed Solana ETFs recorded zero net flows for five consecutive trading days, according to CryptoSlate. The stretch of complete inactivity stands out against the daily inflow or outflow swings typically seen in crypto ETF categories.
stories.whyItMatters: Flat flows across an entire fund category can signal fading investor interest or a wait-and-see posture toward Solana exposure specifically.
whatToWatch: Whether flows resume in either direction in coming days
How Solana ETF flow trends compare with bitcoin and ether ETFs over the same period
questions: Is the zero-flow streak due to genuine lack of demand or a technical/reporting quirk?

stories.title: BlackRock's ETHA reverse split set to undercut Coinbase on trading costs
stories.summary: BlackRock is carrying out a reverse split of its ETHA ether ETF, a move CryptoSlate reports will make trading the fund roughly 70 times cheaper than trading ether directly on Coinbase. Reverse splits raise a fund's per-share price without changing its total value, often used to align share price with peers or narrow trading spreads.
stories.whyItMatters: Lower effective trading costs on a regulated ether ETF could pull volume away from crypto-native exchanges toward traditional brokerage rails.
whatToWatch: The effective date of the reverse split
Whether ETHA trading volume shifts materially versus direct ether trading venues
questions: How was the 70-times cost comparison calculated, and does it hold across different order sizes?

sources.title: BlackRock’s rare ETHA reverse split is about to make trading Ethereum 70 times cheaper than Coinbase

stories.whyItMatters: Departures of senior technical leadership from blockchain infrastructure firms to AI labs highlight competition for talent between the crypto and AI sectors.

stories.summary: Analytics firm CryptoQuant says large holders are accumulating crypto as indicators suggest the current bear market is entering its later stages, according to Cointelegraph. The report frames whale buying as a contrarian signal against prevailing bearish sentiment.
stories.whyItMatters: Whale accumulation during downturns is a metric traders watch for early signs of a market bottom, though it is not a guaranteed predictor.

Price action that confirms or contradicts the 'late-stage bear market' thesis

stories.title: TeraWulf's bitcoin mining revenue drops 73% as AI leases dominate sales
stories.summary: TeraWulf reported a 73% decline in bitcoin mining revenue, with AI-related data center leases now accounting for 71% of total sales, according to CryptoSlate. The figures mark a significant shift in the miner's business mix away from bitcoin mining toward AI infrastructure hosting.
stories.whyItMatters: TeraWulf's pivot reflects a broader trend among publicly traded bitcoin miners diversifying into AI compute hosting as a hedge against tough mining economics.
whatToWatch: TeraWulf's next quarterly results for further shifts in revenue mix
Whether other miners accelerate similar AI leasing pivots
questions: Is the mining revenue decline driven mainly by lower bitcoin prices and network difficulty, or by deliberate capacity reallocation to AI leases?
